title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Customer Service Advisor Customer Service Representative Customer Support Advisor Contact Centre Advisor

Crewe, Cheshire Full-Time 40 Hours per Week 7-Day Rota Variable Shifts

Introduction

Acorn by Synergie is recruiting for Customer Service Advisors to join a growing team in Crewe, Cheshire.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in customer service, contact centres, retail, hospitality or another service-focused environment who enjoys helping people and finding solutions.

You'll handle customer enquiries, understand their needs and take ownership of issues through to resolution, while working as part of a supportive and collaborative team.

If you're a confident communicator who can stay calm under pressure and genuinely enjoys making a difference to customers, we'd like to hear from you.

What We Offer
- Full-time position, 40 hours per week.
- 7-day rota with variable start and finish times.
- Free onsite parking.
- Free access to onsite gym facilities.
- Access to the Acorn by Synergie Worker Wellbeing Programme.
- Acorn by Synergie rewards, discounts and offers scheme.
- Supportive, friendly and inclusive working environment.
- Opportunity to develop your customer service skills within a growing team.

Key Duties
- Handle inbound customer enquiries professionally and with empathy.
- Listen to customers, understand their needs and identify appropriate solutions.
- Take ownership of customer issues and work towards the best possible outcome.
- Provide clear and accurate information using a range of internal systems.
- Resolve queries efficiently while maintaining high customer service standards.
- Work closely with specialist teams when additional support is required.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer records.
- Handle customer information responsibly and maintain high standards of data security.
- Contribute positively to a team environment focused on collaboration and customer satisfaction.

Requirements
- Previous experience in customer service, contact centre, retail, hospitality or another service-based role.
- Excellent verbal communication and active listening skills.
- Positive, professional and customer-focused approach.
- Confident using computers and able to learn new systems quickly.
- Ability to remain calm, organised and professional in a busy environment.
- Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to take ownership of customer queries.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
- Flexible approach to working hours and shift patterns.

Working Hours

The role involves working 40 hours per week across a 7-day rota, with variable start and finish times within the following core opening hours:
- Monday-Friday: 8am-8pm
- Saturday: 9am-6pm
- Sunday: 10am-5pm

You will be required to work one weekend day for two out of every three weekends, with the third weekend fully off.

Interested?

If you're an experienced Customer Service Advisor, Customer Service Representative, Customer Support Advisor, Contact Centre Advisor or Customer Care Advisor looking for your next opportunity in Crewe, apply today with your up-to-date CV.

This role could suit candidates searching for Customer Service Advisor jobs in Crewe, Customer Service jobs in Cheshire, Contact Centre jobs in Crewe, Customer Support jobs in Crewe and Customer Service Representative jobs in Cheshire.

title: Customer Services Administrator
company: Howard James Recruitment Consultancy Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Customer Service Administrator

About the Team

You'll be joining a friendly and supportive team that prides itself on delivering excellent customer service. Working alongside experienced colleagues, you'll receive full training and have the opportunity to develop your skills within a growing business that values teamwork, customer care and continuous improvement.

Due to continued growth, our client is looking to recruit a Customer Service Administrator to support their busy operations team.

The Role

This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the beginning of their career who has gained around 6-12 months' experience in an administration or customer service role and is looking to build their skills in a supportive office environment.

Reporting to the Service Manager, you'll provide day-to-day administrative support while assisting customers with enquiries and ensuring a smooth customer experience. Full training will be provided, so a positive attitude and willingness to learn are just as important as previous experience.

Key Responsibilities
- Respond to customer enquiries via telephone and email.
- Provide excellent customer service and ensure queries are resolved promptly.
- Prepare customer quotations and supporting documentation.
- Update and maintain accurate customer records using the company's internal system.
- Liaise with colleagues and external suppliers to help coordinate customer requests.
- Support the wider team with general administrative tasks.
- Ensure all customer information is recorded accurately and kept up to date.

About You

We're looking for someone who is enthusiastic, organised and enjoys helping people.

Ideally, you'll have:
- 6-12 months' experience in an administration, customer service or office support role.
- A friendly and professional telephone manner.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Basic IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Strong attention to detail and good organisational skills.
- The ability to manage your workload and work to deadlines.
- A positive attitude, willingness to learn and a proactive approach.

What's on Offer

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a growing business that is committed to delivering outstanding customer service while making a positive environmental impact. You'll receive full training, ongoing support and the opportunity to develop your career within a friendly and collaborative team.

title: Operations Administrator

description:

Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will be the first point of contact for members seeking claims advice and support, helping to deliver an exceptional service throughout the lifecycle of a claim. You will also support a range of policy administration activities, including new business enquiries, renewals and policy changes.
This is an excellent opportunity to gain experience in financial services and customer service while working with veterinary professionals across the UK and Ireland. You will collaborate with colleagues across Claims, Underwriting, Finance and IT, developing valuable skills and knowledge in a supportive and professional environment.
What We Offer
At VDS, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We offer a rewarding career, a supportive culture and a comprehensive benefits package, including:
o Competitive salary
o Hybrid working
o 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays
o Private Medical Insurance
o Non-contributory company pension (10% employer contribution)
o Group Life InsurancCashplan with optical, dental and wellbeing allowances
o Employee Assistance Programme
o Charity and volunteering day
o Enhanced family policy, including adoption, maternity, paternity and parental pay
o Buy Holiday and Cycle to Work salary sacrifice schemes

We recognise that skills and experience can be gained in many different ways. If you are excited about this opportunity but do not quite meet every requirement we would still encourage you to apply.
READY TO APPLY?

Apply today and become part of a team that is committed to supporting veterinary professionals and making a real difference every day.
At The Veterinary Defence Society and VDS Training, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is fair, accessible and free from discrimination.

title: Purchasing / Buying Administrator
description:
Purchasing / Buying Administrator

Location: Macclesfield, Cheshire, SK10 2 NZ
Salary: £26,000 £29,000 per annum, DOE
Contract: Full time, permanent

Why Join Us
- Be part of a growing and innovative company where your contributions will truly make a difference.
- Work in a hands-on role that offers a variety of challenges.
- Join a friendly and supportive team with a shared commitment to quality and excellence.
- Competitive salary based on experience
- 25 days holiday, free parking and company pension scheme.

Be Part of a Team Bringing Tomorrow s Electronics to Life!

Are you looking for a role where no two days are the same?

Do you enjoy being at the centre of operations, supporting different teams, and keeping things running smoothly If so, this could be the perfect opportunity for you!

Based at our headquarters in Macclesfield, Cheshire, we have a small multi-disciplined, dynamic team designing and manufacturing high-value robotic machines for testing PCBs (printed circuit boards).

The majority of our sales are to China and the USA, where we operate our own small factories and employ local teams to provide high-quality customer support.

RoBAT is firmly established as the leading company in this very specialised and niche marketplace. This is a unique opportunity to be part of a company at the forefront of industrial automation.

We are looking for a driven and well-organised individual to support our Purchasing, Office and Stores operations. This is a varied role where you ll work closely with our financial, operational and engineering teams.

You ll help manage stock, coordinate purchasing, support administrative activities across the company, and provide a key point of contact for both internal colleagues and external suppliers. Full training will be provided.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys a hands-on, fast-paced environment and wants to grow their skills within an established, supportive team.

As our Purchasing / Buying Administrator you will:
- Manage requisitions and process purchase orders from quotation to delivery
- Liaise with suppliers and internal teams to resolve supply issues
- Coordinate domestic and international shipments (FedEx, UPS, DHL)
- Match delivery notes with purchase orders and record goods received in the ERP system
- Provide administrative support across all departments, including senior leadership
- Act as the first point of contact for phone calls, visitors, and incoming mail
- Maintain office supplies, manage filing, scanning, and data entry tasks
- Update internal records including holiday schedules, absence logs, and fire roll call lists
- Oversee daily operations of the parts store
- Monitor stock levels, reorder supplies and organise inventory
- Conduct regular stock counts and maintain accurate ERP records
- Ensure a clean, safe, and well-organised stores environment

In order to be successful in this role you must have:
- Highly organised, dependable, and detail-driven
- Self-motivated with strong initiative and follow-through
- Confident communicator, both written and verbal
- Proficient with computer systems including Microsoft Excel and ERP platforms
- Strong time-management skills with the ability to prioritise
- Comfortable managing multiple tasks at once
- Positive, collaborative, and eager to learn
- Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities

It would be great if you had:
- Experience in administrative, purchasing, or stores roles
- Exposure to stock control or logistics processes

If you're passionate about mechanical fitting and assembly, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want to contribute to the success of a cutting-edge company, we would love to hear from you!

No agencies please.

title: FM Coordinator
description:
Job description:

My client is a multi-discipline engineering group. Due to their continued growth they are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Coordinator to join their FM team.

Job Description

The Coordinator is responsible for managing and coordinating reactive maintenance requests to ensure repairs are completed efficiently, safely, and within agreed service level agreements (SLAs). The role acts as a key link between Clients, contractors, and internal teams to deliver high-quality maintenance services within building fabric, electrical and mechanical.

Key Responsibilities
- Receive, log, prioritise, and schedule reactive maintenance requests in line with company policies and SLAs
- Assess repair requests to determine urgency, risk, and appropriate response times
- Allocate work to in-house operatives or external contractors and monitor job progress
- Act as the main point of contact for Clients/customers, providing updates and managing expectations
- Liaise with contractors to ensure works are completed on time, within budget, and to required standards
- Ensure all jobs are correctly recorded, closed, and documented on the maintenance management system
- Raise and approve purchase orders in line with financial controls
- Monitor contractor performance and report issues or trends to management
- Ensure compliance with health & safety regulations, including risk assessments and safe systems of work
- Handle complaints or escalations relating to reactive repairs in a professional and timely manner
- Support continuous improvement by identifying recurring issues and recommending preventative actions

Skills & Competencies
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Excellent communication and customer service skills
- Ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks under pressure
- Good understanding of building maintenance and repair processes
- Confident using maintenance management systems ( Verisae / Job Logic ) and Microsoft Office
- Problem-solving mindset with attention to detail
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Knowledge & Experience
- Previous experience in a reactive maintenance, repairs, facilities, or property services role
- Experience coordinating contractors or maintenance operatives
- Knowledge of health & safety legislation relevant to maintenance
- Experience working with SLAs, KPIs, and performance monitoring (desirable)

Qualifications (Desirable)
- NVQ or equivalent in Property, Facilities, or Business Administration
- Customer service or administration qualification

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
- Response and completion times met within SLAs
- Customer satisfaction levels
- First-time fix rates
- Contractor performance and compliance
- Accuracy of job records and system updates

The company offer great opportunities for development and progression within a high profile, growing business

title: Insurance Claims Handler
description:
Senior Claims Handler - EL / PL

Job Market - Liability / Casualty Claims

Senior Claims Handler - EL / PL - About the Role

My client are looking for an experienced Senior Claims Handler - EL/PL to join their specialist liability claims team who manages a diverse portfolio of liability claims on behalf of leading insurers.

As a Senior Claims Handler, you will take ownership of claims from cradle to grave, providing a proactive, technically excellent claims service in line with each insurer's claims philosophy, policy requirements and agreed service standards.

The role will primarily involve handling complex claims above the £25,000 fast-track threshold, requiring strong technical knowledge, sound judgement and excellent negotiation skills.

Senior Claims Handler - EL / PL - Key duties
- Establish policy coverage and confirm whether the appropriate indemnity is in place.
- Accurately record and maintain claims information on the digital claims handling system.
- Proactively investigate liability claims through desk-based investigations and, where appropriate, by instructing loss adjusters and other specialists.
- Assess evidence and make informed decisions on liability.
- Manage claims proactively through to resolution, including negotiating appropriate settlements.
- Ensure claims are handled in accordance with relevant legislation, legal timescales, client SLAs and internal procedures.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with insurers, brokers, solicitors, loss adjusters and other key stakeholders.
- Apply knowledge of policy wordings, terms and conditions when assessing coverage and liability.
- Accurately value personal injury claims and maintain appropriate reserves in line with reserving philosophies.
- Demonstrate a strong understanding of the Civil Procedure Rules and Claims Portal.
- Handle a broad range of Casualty claims, including Personal Injury, Employers' Liability, Public Liability, Construction and Products Liability.
- Apply technical knowledge across relevant UK jurisdictions.
- Authorise claims payments within agreed financial authority limits.
- Support the development of junior colleagues by providing coaching, mentoring and technical guidance.
- Contribute to the continuous improvement of claims-handling standards and processes.

Senior Claims Handler - EL / PL - Key requirements

Strong technical knowledge across a range of EL/PL and Casualty claims.

Experience handling complex and higher-value personal injury claims.

A good understanding of policy coverage, wordings and terms and conditions.

Strong knowledge of the UK insurance market and liability claims environment.

Experience assessing and valuing personal injury claims.

A sound understanding of claims reserving principles.

Knowledge of the Civil Procedure Rules and Claims Portal.

Strong negotiation and decision-making skills.

The ability to manage a caseload proactively from initial notification through to settlement.

Experience working within client SLAs and regulatory/legal deadlines.

Experience within an insurance, claims or legal environment.
